title: Finite scalar coordinates for twisted coherent global sections
statement: Let k be a field, P=Proj k[x_0,x_1] [def-sc-p1-standard], and G a coherent O_P-module [pqf-def-coherent]. For every n in N, there are r in N and an additive equivalence e: Gamma(P,G tensor O_P(n)) -> (Fin r -> k) such that multiplication by any constant homogeneous polynomial C(c) using G tensor twistMul [def-weil-pbc-proj-twisting-sheaf], transported along n+0=n, is sent by e to coordinatewise multiplication by c. The assertion is independent of any representing graded polynomial module.

source.place: Stacks Project, Lemma 01YS(3) and proof of (5), https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/01YS; online text read

proof.text: Equip the twisted global section space S with restriction of scalars along rho, the composite of the degree-zero constant-polynomial equivalence, the inverse affine sections isomorphism and the global-sections map of Proj.toSpecZero. By serreTwistedSectionsFiniteDimensional, S is finite-dimensional for this explicitly constructed module structure.

Set r=Module.finrank k S. The finite basis Module.finBasis k S has a k-linear coordinate equivalence e:S -> (Fin r -> k) by Basis.equivFun. Take its underlying additive equivalence. For c, ha, s and p, serreTwistedSectionsConstantAction rewrites the displayed twistMul section as c*s. The linear equivalence identity e(c*s)=c*e(s) then proves the formula. The finite basis handles dimension zero without a separate case.
